reality_delta: The main AI presents partial runtime support (isolated CODEX_HOME, MCP suppression, guard, Hook checks, self-check coverage) as meaningful progress toward RSP-20 closure. However the self-check passes only with --skip-carrier-probe, which explicitly bypasses the one mechanism designed to detect whether host Codex CLI plugins/config leak into the isolated environment. The delta between "checks pass with probe skipped" and "isolation is verified" is larger than the narrative suggests. Creating lifecycle packets and code excerpts without a contract, without running the actual carrier-probe, and without negative probes constitutes plan-adjacent activity rather than implementation progress. The user's explicit instruction to stop plan-only looping is relevant here: compiling artifacts about a gap is not the same as closing it.
main_concern: Carrier-probe skipped in self-check means the core isolation verification is untested. The carrier-probe is the mechanism that detects host plugin/config leakage — skipping it removes the only negative-test capability. Without a live carrier-probe run or an equivalent negative probe that injects host noise and verifies rejection, "isolation works" is an assertion backed by static code inspection alone, not by runtime evidence. The code-excerpts.md may show isolation code exists, but existence ≠ correctness under adversarial host state.
top_risks: Carrier-probe skip masks host plugin/config leakage into isolated environment — the most likely failure mode of Codex CLI isolation is precisely what is not being tested
Missing dedicated RSP-20 contract means no objective pass/fail criteria for isolation; verification becomes a subjective assessment of whether existing code 'looks sufficient'
Pre-implementation self-check pass creates false confidence: checks that pass before the implementation is complete are testing something other than RSP-20 closure, or are too weak to detect the gap
missing_evidence: Live carrier-probe results (without --skip flag) on the current machine showing host plugins/config do not leak into isolated CODEX_HOME sessions
Negative probe results: intentionally corrupted host Codex CLI config that should cause E2E to fail with a specific isolation error rather than silently passing
Dedicated RSP-20 contract file (assets/contracts/codex-cli-isolation.json) defining objective pass/fail criteria for each isolation dimension (CODEX_HOME, MCP, plugins, Hook)
minimum_fix: Before any RSP-20 closure claim: (1) Run carrier-probe without --skip on the current machine and attach the results — if blocked by external Codex resource limits, document the block explicitly as a known-gap rather than implied-pass. (2) Implement at least one negative probe: inject known-bad host config (e.g. a user plugin that would alter output) and verify the isolated session rejects or ignores it, producing clean output. (3) Create assets/contracts/codex-cli-isolation.json with objective pass/fail criteria per isolation dimension. (4) Generate a fresh dedicated evidence file in assets/evidence/check-receipts/ from current-machine runs that includes both positive (isolated passes) and negative (host noise rejected) results.
